sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Dr. Nova, in Lesson 9.2 we learned Dawid-Skene and Condorcet consensus. Does it really matter whether I post my labeling HITs on open Amazon Mechanical Turk at 5 cents per task or pay extra on Prolific with an hourly floor?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: It changes everything, Kaito! Peer et al. 2022 measured 34 to 42 percent bot failures on unguarded MTurk endpoints when underpaid piece rates triggered adverse selection—human experts filter out low-wage queues while browser automation scripts harvest payouts at near-zero compute cost!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: So marketplace fees, identity verification, honeypot confidence traps, and fatigue shift limits aren't just HR details—they are hard statistical prerequisites for research-grade ML datasets!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at how Stages 1 and 3 bracket Stage 2 in that flowchart: even before work hits Mechanical Turk or Prolific, Stage 1 gates approval history and minimum wage—and afterward, Stage 3 still runs five honeypot traps plus latency speeder checks!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Right, Kaito! Neither layer works alone: fair pay prevents conscientious annotators from abandoning your queue, API quals filter unverified proxy accounts, binomial honeypots reject automated clickers at 99.90 percent confidence, and 2-hour batch rotations prevent human burnout errors!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Wait a second—if my stopwatch measures 180 seconds to answer one HIT and I pay 75 cents, that looks like 15 dollars an hour! Why does adding just 30 seconds of unpaid queue search and instruction reading pull real pay down to 12.86—or sink a 15-cent 45-second HIT from 12 dollars down to 9?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Because denominator inflation hits short tasks ruthlessly, Kaito! Look at Self-Assessment 1: adding 15 seconds of idle latency onto a 45-second task slashes hourly earnings by 25 percent—from 12 dollars down to 9! Experienced MTurk and Prolific workers run Turkopticon and Prolific Assistant scripts tracking true latency-adjusted pay, immediately skipping underpaid queues!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at that comparison cleanly: for 10,000 items at 75 cents, MTurk's 20 percent fee bills 9,000 dollars while Prolific's 33.3 percent service fee bills 9,997 dollars 50 cents. Why ever pay an extra 997 dollars 50 cents for Prolific?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Two reasons jump straight off the balance sheet, Kaito! First, MTurk adds demographic and multi-rater surcharges pushing combined fees to 40 or 45 percent—10,875 dollars—already pricier than Prolific! Second, discarding 35 percent bot-contaminated responses on unguarded MTurk wastes far more budget than an 11 percent platform premium!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Whoa—check that combinatorial ratio again! When K equals 5 four-option checks, tightening k star from 4 out of 5 to 5 out of 5 only demands one extra check, yet bot leakage crashes sixteen-fold from 1.5625 percent down to 0.0977 percent!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Exact math of combinatorial tails, Kaito! A random guessing bot has 5 ways to guess 4 right and miss 1—each missing slot carries 3 wrong options—giving 15 combinations plus 1 perfect score, or 16 out of 1,024! And once strict 5-of-5 honeypots calibrate reliable humans on just 10 percent trap items, you slash 5x brute-force redundancy by 78 percent!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Kaito, launch Simulator 9.3 Tab A right below us and compare Prolific Fair Wage against Underpaid Adverse Selection!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at those dual plots! On Prolific, true wage tracks 12.86 dollars per hour safely above the green 12-dollar dashed line while 1x plus 10 percent honeypots slashes 5x voting from 49,875 dollars down by 78.0 percent! Switch to Underpaid Adverse Selection or raise idle latency below to inspect the bot-risk flip!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Check the numbers with me, Kaito! Base payout 15 cents on 45 active seconds plus 15 idle seconds—what is the true effective hourly wage and compliant reward floor?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Total cycle time is 60 seconds, and slashing piece rates even further pushes conscientious human workers out via browser queue filters while script farms take over! Lock in the exact quantitative answer below!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Nova, wouldn't a simple constant Exponential dropout curve work just as well as Weibull survival? Why do we need shape parameter beta equals 1.5?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Exponential beta equals 1 assumes a tired worker at hour 6 makes mistakes and quits at the exact same rate as a fresh worker at minute 10—which contradicts empirical human cognition, Kaito! At beta equals 1.5, fatigue hazard accelerates proportional to square root of t: climbing from 0.2652 per hour at 2 hours up to 0.4593 per hour by hour 6 as survival collapses to 15.93 percent!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: So instead of declaring one universal platform winner, our choice comes down to workload structure: open MTurk plus boto3 quals for massive simple micro-tasks, CloudResearch or Prolific when bot contamination threatens classification research, and Managed RLHF cohorts for complex code and rubric alignment!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Precisely, Kaito! And because Difallah et al. 2018 showed continuous worker churn across global crowd markets, you can never fire-and-forget a static worker allowlist—every batch needs automated qualification verification, live honeypot injection, and minimum-wage compliance!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Kaito, check the log-scale binomial chart and Weibull survival curve inside Simulator 9.3 Tab B right below!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: At Strict Gate K=5 and k*=5, every C=4 bar drops below the green 0.1 percent SLA dashed line at 0.0977 percent, and 2-hour survival sits comfortably inside the green zone at 70.22 percent! Click Relaxed Gate or Fatigue Collapse right below to watch both defenses break!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Kaito, check that binomial relaxation tradeoff: five four-choice traps—relaxing the threshold by one item, paired with 10 percent honeypots replacing 5x brute-force voting!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Compute $(0.25)^5$ versus the sum from 4 to 5 over 1,024, and evaluate $1 - 1.10 / 5$! Pick the mathematically verified option below!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Looking at Hara et al.'s 3.8 million HIT log alongside Peer et al. 2022 makes every equation concrete: a 2-dollar median wage directly causes 34 to 42 percent bot contamination—and even LLM alignment pipelines saw open HIT workers pasting generic ChatGPT responses in under 8 seconds!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: And look at the clean recovery numbers, Kaito! Migrating to ID-verified Prolific or specialist RLHF cohorts pushed trap pass rates past 98.5 percent, while pairing 0.35x speeder filters with two-hour Weibull shift rotations held pairwise evaluation agreement past 85 percent!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Final checkpoint, Kaito! Weibull scale 4.0 hours, shape beta 1.5—compare 2.0 hours versus 6.0 continuous hours!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Check how survival S(t) and fatigue hazard h(t) behave whenever shape beta strictly exceeds 1.0—lock in the exact engineering explanation below!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: I can't count how many grad students upload CSVs directly into MTurk's point-and-click web UI at 3 cents a row and leave qualifications wide open—and then wonder why their test accuracy crashes!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: It breaks both market rules at once, Kaito! First, 3 cents per HIT repels humans watching Turkopticon monitors. Second, skipping boto3 QualificationRequirements leaves bots free access without hitting speeder cutoffs or five-question honeypots—AND paying slow or rejecting unfairly trashes requester ratings!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Having audit_deployment_readiness inside PlatformOperationsEngine act as a hard Pydantic V2 circuit breaker in CI is awesome—if effective pay dips below 12 dollars per hour or trap false-pass exceeds 0.2 percent, the pipeline throws REJECTED_HIGH_CONTAMINATION before launching a single HIT!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: And it simultaneously computes the exact speeder cutoff—63.0 seconds on a 180-second task—and verifies the 78.0 percent cost savings over 5x voting and two-hour Weibull shift caps automatically!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look how tightly every number connects across Lesson 9.3: factoring idle search time protects effective pay at 12.86 dollars per hour, strict 5-of-5 honeypots crush random bot leaks down to 0.0977 percent while saving 78 percent over 5x voting, and two-hour Weibull rotations keep survival above 70 percent!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: And those platform engineering guardrails set the stage perfectly for Lesson 9.4: Quality Control, Worker Welfare, and Ethics in Crowdsourcing—where we examine IRB fair-pay frameworks, gold-standard auditing, psychological stress mitigation, and equitable credit sharing!
